articles.title: Running SEO Checks in a CI Pipeline: What to Automate
articles.excerpt: The deploy went green. Every test passed. Two days later, someone in marketing posted a Search Console screenshot in Slack: pages were dropping out of the index. A template change had shipped a noinde…
articles.body: The deploy went green. Every test passed. Two days later, someone in marketing posted a Search Console screenshot in Slack: pages were dropping out of the index. A template change had shipped a noindex tag that was only ever meant for staging. Nothing in the pipeline caught it, because nothing in the pipeline was looking. Unit tests check that your code behaves. They don't check the HTML that Googlebot actually receives. This post is a practical plan for running SEO checks in a CI pipeline. It covers which checks to automate, where each one should run, and which ones to leave to humans. Every script below was tested before publishing, and you can drop them into a GitHub Actions setup today. If you've wanted to start automated SEO testing but weren't sure where the line was, this is it.

articles.body: Airbyte title matches are candidates until the control plane is confirmed A data-integration platform is a high-value control plane because a user can configure where credentials and records travel. Finding internet-visible Airbyte services helps an organization review ownership and authentication. A broad title match, however, is not proof of a confirmed Airbyte deployment and should never be presented as one. On 2026-10-28 at 21:41 UTC, a ZoomEye SDK probe used sub_type=all , page 1, and a page size of one. The query app="Airbyte" returned 1 match. The title query title="Airbyte" returned 12,861. The wide difference shows the limits of both observations.

articles.title: Best AI Code Review Tools by False Positive Rate (2026): What the Benchmarks Actually Show
articles.excerpt: I design review pipelines, and every vendor I talk to quotes a false positive number. None of them agree, because each 2026 benchmark defines a false positive its own way. I read six benchmarks and fi…
articles.body: I design review pipelines, and every vendor I talk to quotes a false positive number. None of them agree, because each 2026 benchmark defines a false positive its own way. I read six benchmarks and five tools' docs in October 2026 to learn what the numbers mean and which tools act on noise. TL;DR Benchmarks disagree because each one defines "wrong" differently. In one 2026 study, developers rejected most of a widely used reviewer's comments, with false positives a main reason ( arXiv 2607.03316 , July 2026), while CR-Bench counts even correct comments against precision (arXiv 2603.11078, March 2026). Precision without recall hides missed bugs.

articles.title: Best AI Code Review Tools for Air-Gapped and Self-Hosted Environments (2026)
articles.excerpt: Air-gapped AI code review means the whole review, model calls included, runs with nothing crossing your network boundary. I design review pipelines for teams whose code can't leave the building, and I…
articles.body: Air-gapped AI code review means the whole review, model calls included, runs with nothing crossing your network boundary. I design review pipelines for teams whose code can't leave the building, and I checked five tools against their own docs on October 27 and 28, 2026, ranking them on what a review sends over the wire. TL;DR Self-hosted and air-gapped mean different things. A self-hosted reviewer can still call a hosted model over the internet, and an air-gapped one can't call anything outside your network. The test is zero egress with your own model endpoint. A tool passes when the review runs, model calls included, with no route out, and still reads more than the diff. Most regulated teams already find sovereignty hard.

articles.title: 5 days beneath the waves: What it's like to live in an underwater 'space station'
articles.excerpt: Confined inside a research station 22 feet (7 meters) underwater, Analog Astronaut Commander Dr. Musilova and her crew performed research and maintenance activities like future astronauts on Mars.
articles.body: Living underwater was surprisingly peaceful. It was in many ways exactly what I imagine living on Mars would be like one day. There were no humans around us, except for my three SEA STAR crewmembers and me. Apart from the human noises we made, we couldn't hear anything other than the life support systems keeping us alive submerged 22 feet (7 meters) below the surface. We were living in these extreme conditions to study the challenges astronauts may face on long-duration space missions. Since performing research in space is still rare and expensive, there are numerous facilities around the world that focus on recreating space-like conditions on Earth . One of those stations is the Jules' Undersea Lab, where the SEA STAR simulated space mission took place.

articles.title: ISS astronaut will conduct Canada's 1st spacewalk in 7 years on Oct. 29: Watch it live
articles.excerpt: Joshua Kutryk will venture outside the International Space Station on Oct. 29, on the first spacewalk by a Canadian astronaut in more than seven years. Here's how to watch it live.
articles.body: The next International Space Station (ISS) spacewalk will have more maple-leaf flavor than usual, as a Canadian astronaut will become the first to go outside the orbiting complex in seven years. Canadian Space Agency (CSA) astronaut Joshua Kutryk, who's also a colonel in the Royal Canadian Air Force, will help the ISS boost its power supply during his first-ever spacewalk on Thursday (Oct. 29). Kutryk will be joined by NASA astronaut Anil Menon, who has done three spacewalks already and also serves as a colonel with the U.S. Space Force . The duo are scheduled to venture outside the orbiting lab at 8 a.m. EDT (1200 GMT), kicking off a spacewalk that will last roughly 6 hours and 45 minutes. You can watch it live here at Space.com , courtesy of NASA, beginning at 6:30 a.m. EDT (1030 GMT).
